articles.title: In 1985, a British comedy fundraiser began with a televised appeal; 40 years later, Comic Relief has raised over £1.6 billion to tackle poverty worldwide
articles.summary: A British comedy fundraiser that began with a televised appeal in 1985 has grown into one of the country's best-known charitable initiatives, raising more
articles.body: A British comedy fundraiser that began with a televised appeal in 1985 has grown into one of the country's best-known charitable initiatives, raising more than £1.6 billion over four decades. Founded amid the humanitarian crisis caused by famine in Ethiopia, Comic Relief brought comedians and entertainers together to encourage people to donate to those in need. Its flagship campaign, Red Nose Day, launched in 1988 and turned comedy, celebrity performances and public participation into a recurring fundraising event. Over the years, the charity has supported thousands of projects in the UK and internationally, helping organisations tackle poverty, improve access to essential services and support vulnerable communities. What began as an unconventional fundraising idea has become a long-running movement combining entertainment with charitable giving.How Comic Relief began in 1985Comic Relief was established in 1985 against the backdrop of the devastating famine in Ethiopia and the wider humanitarian crisis in East Africa. Its origins are associated with British screenwriter Richard Curtis, comedian Lenny Henry and charity entrepreneur Jane Tewson.According to Comic Relief's historical annual report, the organisation was launched on Christmas Day 1985 through a satellite broadcast from a refugee camp in Sudan. The appeal sought to draw attention to the humanitarian crisis and encourage support for people affected by poverty and displacement.The founders developed an approach that used comedy and entertainment to engage audiences with charitable causes. Rather than relying exclusively on conventional appeals, they sought to make fundraising accessible to a broad public through humour, television and collective participation.The first Red Nose Day raised £15 millionThree years after Comic Relief was established, its flagship fundraising campaign, Red Nose Day, was launched in 1988. The first event combined comedy sketches, television appearances and public fundraising to encourage donations for people facing poverty and hardship.According to Comic Relief's official history, the inaugural Red Nose Day raised approximately £15 million. The televised event featured comedy performances involving Blackadder and The Young Ones, helping establish a format that would become a recurring feature of British television and popular culture.The red nose became the campaign's recognisable symbol, giving supporters a simple way to participate and show their support. Over time, the event expanded to include celebrity challenges, community activities, merchandise and donations from individuals and businesses.How comedy became a fundraising toolComic Relief built its approach around the idea that entertainment could encourage people to engage with serious social issues. Comedy sketches, celebrity appearances and fundraising challenges became central features of its televised campaigns.Over the years, the charity has encouraged people to organise activities in schools, workplaces and communities. Supporters have raised money through sponsored challenges, bake sales, merchandise and individual donations, alongside the major televised appeals.In 2002, Comic Relief launched Sport Relief, a fundraising initiative that encouraged people to participate in sporting and physical activities to support charitable causes. The initiative broadened the charity's fundraising approach beyond comedy and television performances.The combination of entertainment and public participation helped Comic Relief sustain its fundraising activities over several decades, bringing charitable causes to audiences who might not otherwise have engaged with traditional appeals.Comic Relief crossed £1 billion in fundraisingA major milestone came in 2015, when Comic Relief announced that its cumulative fundraising had exceeded £1 billion. The announcement coincided with the 30th anniversary of the organisation's founding.Red Nose Day 2015 raised £99,418,831, according to the charity's official historical records. The campaign featured comedy performances, celebrity appearances and fundraising challenges designed to encourage public donations.In 2022, Comic Relief announced that its cumulative fundraising had surpassed £1.5 billion. That year's Red Nose Day raised £42,790,147, marking another significant milestone in the organisation's history.By its 40th anniversary in 2025, Comic Relief reported that it had raised more than £1.6 billion over four decades. This was the cumulative amount raised since the organisation's launch in 1985, rather than the proceeds from a single televised event.Where the money goesComic Relief directs funding towards organisations working to tackle poverty and social injustice in the UK and internationally. Its grants support projects addressing immediate needs as well as programmes intended to improve people's circumstances over the longer term.The charity's funding priorities include helping people access food and safe accommodation, supporting children and young people, protecting vulnerable communities and addressing inequalities. Its work also covers issues such as homelessness, mental health, domestic violence and access to essential services.Rather than delivering every service directly, Comic Relief works with organisations that understand the needs of the communities they serve. These organisations use grants to provide support, develop programmes and address challenges affecting disadvantaged people.The charity's approach recognises that poverty can involve several interconnected problems, including inadequate housing, limited access to education, poor health and exposure to violence. Funding initiatives that address these challenges is central to its stated ambition of working towards a world free from poverty.Red Nose Day marked 40 years in 2025In 2025, Comic Relief celebrated the 40th anniversary of its founding. The anniversary campaign looked back at four decades of fundraising while encouraging the public to continue supporting its work.Red Nose Day 2025 raised £34,022,590, according to Comic Relief's official records. The televised event featured comedy sketches, celebrity appearances and fundraising challenges.Among the participants was Jamie Laing, who completed five consecutive ultramarathons, raising £2,053,835. Former racing driver Billy Monger also undertook the Ironman World Championship challenge, raising £1,287,259 for the charity.Comic Relief said it had raised more than £1.6 billion and supported over 100 million people during its first 40 years. The anniversary highlighted how an initiative that began with a televised appeal had developed into an established fundraising organisation supporting communities in the UK and around the world.The campaign continues beyond its anniversaryComic Relief continued its fundraising activities in 2026. According to its official history, Red Nose Day 2026 raised £30,004,040 to support people in need.The televised event was hosted by Davina McCall, Joel Dommett, Katherine Ryan, Nick Mohammed and Catherine Tate. Broadcaster Greg James undertook a 1,000-kilometre tandem cycling challenge from Weymouth to Edinburgh, raising £4,225,939.Comic Relief said the overall fundraising total would help more than 1.3 million people access essential support, including food, shelter and safety.Four decades after its launch, Comic Relief continues to use comedy to draw attention to poverty and encourage charitable giving. Its history illustrates how an unconventional fundraising idea can develop into a long-running campaign, bringing together entertainers, communities and donors to support people facing hardship.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Kansas man’s animal drawings attracted millions of followers; his family now sells colouring books, T-shirts and mugs featuring his art
articles.summary: A Kansas artist’s animal drawings have attracted millions of social media followers, helping turn his creative hobby into a family-run business selling
articles.body: A Kansas artist’s animal drawings have attracted millions of social media followers, helping turn his creative hobby into a family-run business selling books, colouring products and merchandise. Trent Landreth, known online as Drawings by Trent, has 2 million followers on Facebook, 1.3 million on Instagram and 3 million on TikTok. His popularity began with a video of him drawing animals on a trampoline with chalk, shared by his mother around ten years ago. His parents now help record his videos, manage the business and sell products featuring his artwork, including colouring books, stickers, T-shirts and mugs.How did a Kansas artist’s animal drawings become an online sensationLandreth first went viral around ten years ago, when his mother shared a video of him drawing animals on a trampoline with chalk. The video showed him sketching animals including an elephant, an alligator and a gorilla, while cicadas could be heard in the background. According to KMUW, a National Public Radio member station based in Wichita, Kansas, he gained his first million followers over the following four months. His parents, however, say that he is not aware of the extent of his online popularity and does not draw to entertain other people.His family has continued sharing his drawings through social media, where viewers can watch him respond to drawing requests. Away from the camera, Landreth produces more detailed artwork using black ballpoint pens, with phone books serving as his preferred drawing surface. His mother explained that the soft pages allow the pen to leave a groove that he can feel as he draws. She also suggested that he enjoys the busy appearance of phone book pages, which differ from the cleaner surfaces of conventional sketchbooks.What products does Drawings by Trent sell featuring his animal artworkLandreth’s online following has helped his family establish a business selling products featuring his artwork. Drawings by Trent offers colouring books, stickers, T-shirts, mugs and three published books. His parents help manage the operation, using space in their family home to store merchandise, prepare orders and package products for customers. When Landreth packs an order himself, the package receives a special sticker so that customers can identify his involvement.The business is also intended to help provide for Landreth in the future, when his parents may no longer be able to care for him. According to KMUW, the family’s wider mission is to demonstrate the value of including people with different needs in everyday life. His father, Corey Landreth, said: “When we share our lives, we are not just helping those ‘poor’ special needs individuals. We actually grow and become better people.” The family has also spoken about the importance of representing Landreth carefully, rather than assuming how he feels about his experiences.What is Trent’s View of the Zoo, and why is it a best-selling colouring bookOne of Landreth’s most successful products is Trent’s View of the Zoo, his first colouring book, which remains a best-seller for the business. His artwork has also led to collaborations with companies and other creators. KMUW reported that he helped design artwork for the children’s menu at the restaurant chain Old Chicago. He also collaborated with Tanner Smith, known from Netflix’s Love on the Spectrum, on a T-shirt collection with Vineyard Vines for Autism Acceptance Month.The family is preparing to expand its publishing work with a new activity book expected early in 2027. According to KMUW, the book is planned to be available at Walmart stores nationwide. Landreth also travels with his parents for meet-and-greet events, where he interacts with fans from across the United States. His family says he enjoys these trips, particularly staying in hotels and exploring new accommodations. Alongside his drawing and business activities, he frequently visits his local public library and spends much of his time with his family.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 'Dedication and ingenuity of our space scientists': PM Modi hails ISRO after successful GSLV-F18 launch carrying NVS-03
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday congratulated Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) scientists and engineers following the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday congratulated Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) scientists and engineers following the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission carrying the NVS-03 navigation satellite, saying the mission would strengthen India's indigenous satellite navigation system, NavIC.In a post on X, PM Modi said, "Congratulations to our scientists and engineers at ISRO on the successful launch of GSLV-F18 carrying NVS-03.Also read: Success launch of navigation sat NVS-03 with desi atomic clock will make NaVIC up & running, and give military strategic independenceThis mission marks an important step in strengthening NavIC, our indigenous satellite navigation system. Equipped with enhanced capabilities, NVS-03 will further our pursuit of self-reliance in critical technologies and support navigation services that benefit our people.The dedication and ingenuity of our space scientists continue to make our nation proud."The successful launch is expected to strengthen India's strategic autonomy by helping restore the operational capabilities of NavIC, India's indigenous alternative to global navigation systems such as the US-operated GPS and Russia's GLONASS.The NVS-03 satellite carries an indigenously developed atomic clock, alongside imported atomic clocks, marking an important step towards reducing India's dependence on foreign technologies for satellite-based navigation. Atomic clocks provide highly precise time signals that are essential for determining location, navigation and timing.NavIC, which was originally designed around a seven-satellite constellation, had been operating with only three active satellites, below the minimum requirement of four satellites for standalone positioning services. This had limited its use for critical applications, including military navigation, precision positioning and coordination of naval assets.An operational NavIC constellation is particularly important for India's armed forces, which require reliable Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) signals for missile guidance, precision-guided weapons, troop movement, combat aircraft and naval operations.Dependence on foreign navigation networks can pose strategic vulnerabilities during conflicts, as access to such services could potentially be restricted or disrupted. India experienced the limitations of relying on foreign satellite navigation systems during the 1999 Kargil war.With NVS-03, India aims to strengthen the availability of indigenous navigation services for both civilian and strategic applications. NavIC is designed to provide coverage across India and up to 1,500 km beyond its geographical boundaries.The original NavIC constellation comprised seven satellites supported by a network of ground stations operating round the clock. Three satellites were placed in geostationary orbit, while four were placed in inclined geosynchronous orbits.However, the constellation's operational strength declined over time as ageing satellites could not be replaced as planned. The launch of NVS-02 on January 29, 2025, also failed to deliver the intended results after a pyro valve signal loss in the engine prevented the satellite from reaching its designated orbit.The successful deployment of NVS-03 is expected to address some of these operational limitations and strengthen India's efforts to establish an independent satellite navigation capability.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Alaska Airlines to cut 200 jobs as Iran war-driven fuel costs threaten $700 million loss
articles.summary: Alaska Air Group will eliminate around 200 non-contract positions as soaring fuel prices and geopolitical tensions linked to the Iran war put pressure on
articles.body: Alaska Air Group will eliminate around 200 non-contract positions as soaring fuel prices and geopolitical tensions linked to the Iran war put pressure on its finances, with the airline warning it could suffer losses of up to $700 million this year.The job cuts, announced on Friday, signal how the fuel-price shock triggered by the Iran war is beginning to affect employment in the US aviation industry, with carriers already raising airfares and scaling back expansion plans to offset higher operating costs.In a memo to employees, Chief Executive Ben Minicucci said the company could report an adjusted pretax loss of as much as $700 million in 2026 if current conditions persist. This would mark its first adjusted pretax loss outside the Covid-19 pandemic since 2003, Reuters reported."We must return to the financial discipline that has long been a key competitive advantage," Minicucci said, adding that overhead expenses had "grown at a disproportionate rate to revenue" in recent years.The reductions will affect less than 1% of Alaska Air's approximately 32,500 employees. These include 125 positions in Washington state and 48 in Hawaii. The company said no frontline or non-management jobs would be eliminated.Affected employees will have November 13 as their last working day but will continue receiving pay through December 31, along with severance and other support, according to the memo.Expansion plans face financial pressureThe Seattle-based airline is pursuing an ambitious expansion into premium and international travel following its acquisition of Hawaiian Airlines. Its strategy includes investments in premium cabins, loyalty programmes and new international routes, with plans to expand its long-haul network from Seattle.Minicucci said the company would continue investing in its fleet, customer experience and network despite tightening spending elsewhere.You use AI every day. articles.title: A first-grade teacher in Kansas started ending each day with children repeating positive affirmations; the simple routine spread beyond his classroom as other teachers adopted the idea
articles.summary: Someone truly said that a teacher can change a thousand lives.
articles.body: Someone truly said that a teacher can change a thousand lives. One such example is an elementary school teacher from Kansas, who came up with a simple idea of ending each school day with children repeating positive affirmations. What began as a small classroom routine soon caught on, inspiring other teachers across the school to adopt the practice.At a time when conversations around children’s education often revolve around academic performance, grades, dress codes and whatnot, this simple initiative offers a gentle reminder that just a few words of encouragement can become an opportunity for children to recognise their own strengths and leave school feeling valued and with a sense of belonging.How one teacher's idea spread across the schoolTyler Richards, a first-grade teacher at Rex Elementary School in Haysville, Kansas, has been receiving appreciation for his simple approach to ending the school day. Before leaving the classroom, his young students repeat positive affirmations, including phrases such as “I am kind” and “I can do hard things”.The idea might feel simple and ordinary at first, but its purpose goes beyond having children memorise a few encouraging sentences. By repeating these words together, students get an opportunity to remind themselves that they can be kind, face challenges and approach new situations with confidence. Moreover, this small gesture creates a lasting bond between students and their teacher, allowing students to trust and depend on their teachers even outside academics.The idea soon caught the attention of the school’s principal, Shane Paulus, who appreciated the way it helped children feel welcomed and valued. Speaking about the practice, Paulus told KSN News that it was a good way for students to feel loved and appreciated before heading home and to end their day on a positive note.What makes the story particularly heartwarming is how quickly the idea travelled beyond Richards' own classroom. Teachers across different grades at Rex Elementary began introducing similar practices, allowing more children to participate in the daily exercise.According to the report by Good News Network, students themselves have also started taking ownership of the initiative by suggesting new ways to put the practice into action. This response suggests that the routine has become more than something children are instructed to do. Instead, they are beginning to own it as something of their own.Why positive affirmations can matter during childhoodChildhood is a period when children gradually develop an understanding of themselves, their abilities and their relationships with others. Along the way, they encounter new experiences, make mistakes, struggle with unfamiliar tasks and learn how to navigate friendships. The way adults respond to these encounters shapes how children view their own capabilities.Positive affirmations not only remind children of their own strengths but also assure them that the adults around them trust them, value them and consider them individuals. These affirmations remind them that there is more to life than failures. For a young child, even a seemingly simple challenge can feel like the end of the world. Whether it is starting a new semester or making new friends, these messages encourage children to focus on positive aspects of themselves.Of course, repeating affirmations is not a substitute for good teaching, emotional and personal guidance, or addressing the difficulties a child may be experiencing. Children also need adults who listen to them, acknowledge their feelings and help them work through problems. Encouraging words are most meaningful when they are reinforced by everyday experiences in which children feel respected and supported.A small classroom habit with a larger messageOne of the significant aspects of this initiative is its emphasis on making children feel that they belong. For young students, school is not only where they learn academic skills. It is also where they build relationships with teachers, interact with classmates and begin to understand how they fit into a larger community.Richards has emphasised the importance of creating a safe place for children. Children spend a significant amount of their day at school. This is an important part of the story because a child's experience of school extends beyond what happens during a lesson.When children feel comfortable asking questions, making mistakes and seeking help, they have more opportunities to participate in the classroom. A welcoming environment cannot be created through affirmations alone, but small gestures of reassurance can form part of a broader effort to build that environment.There is also a lesson here for parents and caregivers. Encouragement does not always have to come in the form of elaborate praise or rewards. Reminding children that they can learn from mistakes, that kindness matters and that asking for help is acceptable can become part of everyday conversations at home. The most important thing parents often forget is that their children are also individuals with their own personalities and emotions and must be treated as such.Ultimately, Richards' initiative is a reminder that teaching involves more than helping children understand what is written in their textbooks. It also involves creating an environment in which they feel seen, supported and encouraged to grow. Sometimes, it is a small idea that makes a big difference.You use AI every day. articles.title: A couple spent years restoring a 170-year-old Wisconsin grain mill into a 4,388-square-foot home; the historic property is reportedly sold for $750,000
articles.summary: A deteriorating grain mill in rural Wisconsin was given a second life as a country home after years of work by Ross and Theresa Halverson, who had
articles.body: A deteriorating grain mill in rural Wisconsin was given a second life as a country home after years of work by Ross and Theresa Halverson, who had backgrounds as antiques dealers. In December 2010, the mill’s then-owner told Ross Halverson that he planned to demolish the building. Halverson took it on the condition that he move it, and the structure was relocated roughly a mile in March 2011. The mill, which dates to the 1850s, needed extensive repairs, including work on floors that were unsafe to walk on. The couple adapted the former industrial building for residential use while retaining elements of its original materials and machinery. Its renovated interior combined an open layout, vintage furnishings and a farmhouse-style kitchen. The property at 33511 Old Mill Drive in Lone Rock, Wisconsin, was later marketed as a furnished historic mill conversion. Shorewest’s listing search reports a sale for $750,000 on October 9, 2026, but the transaction has not been independently confirmed.How a historic mill was moved across Wisconsin farmlandAccording to The Capital Times, the building began its move at 4:30 a.m. on March 8, 2011. The report described plans to transport it across fields while the ground was still frozen. The mill’s construction date is uncertain. The real-estate listing dates it to 1856, while a local historian quoted by The Capital Times and a Wisconsin State Farmer columnist both identify 1858 as the construction year.After the move, the Halversons faced extensive work to make the building suitable for everyday living. Its floors were unsafe to walk on, and the restoration involved replacing the roof, improving insulation and rebuilding the flooring. The couple also removed old equipment and reused original materials wherever possible. In a Country Living feature, Theresa Halverson recalled that it took 4 years before they could sleep in the building. The couple moved in during late 2015, according to Wisconsin State Farmer, roughly 4½ years after the March 2011 relocation.Inside the converted mill: salvaged materials and farmhouse detailsAccording to Country Living, the restored mill has an open, atrium-like layout across its lower 2 floors, tall ceilings and white walls. The owners combined these features with vintage furnishings and repurposed components from the building’s industrial past. Ross Halverson used salvaged materials to make furniture and decorative pieces, including a dining table incorporating old porch posts and parts from a flour-making machine. Industrial remnants also became interior features, while an old storm door was repurposed as a coffee table.The kitchen features white cabinetry, an apron-front sink and butcher-block countertops. In the pantry, Theresa displayed her collection of jadeite dishes. In a bedroom sitting area, shelves hold collections of ironstone and pottery. The bedrooms use neutral fabrics and painted furniture. Ross painted a four-poster bed white, and Theresa dressed it with cream-coloured bedding. A whitewashed antique cupboard provides linen storage. Photographer Annie Schlechter photographed the property for Country Living.Wisconsin grain mill reportedly sells for $750,000The property at 33511 Old Mill Drive in Lone Rock was marketed as a historic mill conversion with 2 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms and 4,388 square feet, according to the real-estate listing. The site covers 2.39 acres and includes a barn with heated workshop space and a separate blacksmith shop. Marketing material described the property as a furnished home with original mill gearing and industrial features retained. The listing also promoted potential uses including short-term accommodation, retreats and events, subject to applicable local requirements.The property has appeared in listings at different asking prices. Country Living reported in September 2025 that the Halversons had put the home on the market, and an earlier listing from another brokerage advertised it for $1.2 million. The earliest listing record located for the later price sequence dates to December 2025, when the asking price was $849,900. Subsequent prices included $799,900 and $784,900. Shorewest’s listing search reports that the property sold for $750,000 on October 9, 2026. However, a Weichert page continued to show it at $784,900. Because the transaction has not been confirmed through a primary property record or the listing agent, the reported sale price and date should be treated with caution.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Dosas, Diwali and temple visits: US midterm candidates step up outreach to Indian-American voters
articles.summary: As the US midterm campaign gathers pace, Indian-American communities are increasingly finding themselves in the spotlight, with candidates turning to
articles.body: As the US midterm campaign gathers pace, Indian-American communities are increasingly finding themselves in the spotlight, with candidates turning to cultural events, temple visits and even dosa-making sessions to connect with voters who could influence the outcome of closely fought contests.In suburban Dallas, Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico recently traded campaign appearances for a cooking lesson at an Indian restaurant in Irving, an area with a sizeable Indian-American population.Dressed in a black suit and white shirt, Talarico was seen scooping dosa batter from a bowl, spreading it across a hot pan and topping it with a spicy potato filling. He then folded the crispy dosa and served it on a banana leaf-lined plate, drawing applause from those present.The outreach comes as Talarico mounts a strong challenge to Republican nominee Ken Paxton in the Senate race in traditionally Republican Texas.Temples and Diwali celebrations become campaign stopsRestaurants are not the only places where candidates are seeking to connect with Indian-American voters. Hindu temples and community celebrations have increasingly featured in their outreach efforts, particularly in states with large Indian-American populations.Connecticut Governor Ned Lamont, who is seeking another term, joined Diwali celebrations organised at the State Capitol alongside Deputy Secretary of State Jennifer Barahona.In Ohio, Congressman Greg Landsman attended the 11th Patotsav celebrations at the BAPS Swaminarayan Temple in Sharonville, marking the anniversary of its consecration.New Jersey Senator Cory Booker also participated in Diwali celebrations at the Akshardham temple, while Congressmen Randy Fine and Scott Perry visited a temple in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania.In Michigan, Congressman John James visited a Swaminarayan temple to learn about its traditions and understand the spirit of service within the Hindu-American community.With even a one- or two-percentage-point shift potentially influencing the outcome in competitive races, candidates are increasingly looking to build connections with Indian-American communities through cultural events, religious gatherings and direct engagement.You use AI every day. articles.title: Fake US voters? China-linked accounts flood X with divisive posts ahead of midterms
articles.summary: A China-linked influence operation known as Spamouflage is active ahead of the US midterm elections, with accounts allegedly posing as American voters and
articles.body: A China-linked influence operation known as Spamouflage is active ahead of the US midterm elections, with accounts allegedly posing as American voters and circulating divisive political content on X. The findings were reported by New York-based social media intelligence firm Graphika, which tracks online influence networks.In a blog post published on Friday, Graphika said it had identified a network of accounts linked to the long-running operation that were posting content targeting US politics, social issues and the electoral process. The activity, it said, closely resembled tactics documented ahead of the 2024 US presidential election.“The accounts post content questioning election integrity and the legitimacy of US democracy,” Graphika said in its blog.The findings come amid longstanding warnings from US intelligence and national security officials about foreign influence operations targeting American voters. Russia, China and Iran have previously been identified as countries running online campaigns aimed at shaping political narratives and influencing public opinion.However, analysts, quoted by news agency AP, have said China's approach has largely focused on undermining public confidence in US democratic institutions rather than supporting one presidential candidate over another.China has rejected allegations of election interference. Liu Chang, spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy in Washington, said Beijing “has never and will never interfere in the US elections."Despite the concerns raised by Graphika, some researchers have questioned the network's ability to influence mainstream political opinion. Darren Linvill, who co-directs Clemson University's Watt Family Innovation Center Media Forensics Hub and has tracked Spamouflage activity, said the operation was unlikely to sway political discussions.“There is no chance it tips the balance in any real political conversation,” Linvill told AP.“Spamouflage is famously bad at mimicking real Americans," he added. “It's outside their wheelhouse.”Linvill said the network's impact was more evident in its efforts to suppress information and target individuals, particularly members of the Chinese diaspora.The accounts linked to the operation “very frequently attack and harass members of the Chinese diaspora community”, he said, describing the activity as part of a wider effort by Beijing to silence views it opposes.Graphika also identified specific accounts that appeared to have changed their identities or content strategies to target US political audiences.The firm also flagged four accounts with a history of Spamouflage activity that have since adopted MAGA-style personas, amplifying content associated with the political movement.Another account, which has more than 2,00,000 followers and presents itself as a Philippine culture blog, was found posting pro-China material alongside divisive content focused on US politics.Graphika said it could not establish whether the account had been hijacked, sold or otherwise transferred to a different operator, leaving questions about who currently controls it.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Georgia man bought 7.25 acres for $89,000, but the house he planned to sell stood on a separate one-acre plot; a court upheld the disputed sale of both
articles.summary: A Georgia appeals court has upheld a ruling in a property dispute involving a house built across two adjoining plots, after a deed mistakenly excluded the
articles.body: A Georgia appeals court has upheld a ruling in a property dispute involving a house built across two adjoining plots, after a deed mistakenly excluded the one-acre parcel on which most of the residence stood. Carson Blackwell purchased 7.25 acres in Gwinnett County for $89,000 in 2014, later acquiring the neighbouring acre for $13,000 to build a house. When the combined property was sold in 2018, the transfer documents listed only the original 7.25 acres. On 20 October 2026, the Georgia Court of Appeals affirmed a lower court’s decision to correct the deeds.Georgia landowner purchased adjoining acre to build a houseBlackwell initially bought the undeveloped 7.25-acre parcel in Gwinnett County, intending to construct a house there. Environmental and soil studies revealed that building on the land as it stood would be prohibitively expensive, prompting him to purchase the separate one-acre plot for $13,000. He subsequently prepared plans showing the proposed house and septic drain field across both parcels. Gwinnett County approved a combination plat, assigned the combined property a single tax identification number and address, and Blackwell recorded the plat before proceeding with construction.House sale documents listed 7.25 acres instead of the combined propertyThe house remained unfinished when Blackwell transferred the larger parcel to his business, The Right Touch Painters LLC, in 2018. The company later agreed to sell the property to RW Investments LLC for $700,000, with the agreement describing a house that would be completed before closing. The sale documents and associated security deed, however, identified only the original 7.25-acre parcel. The omission became significant because the house stood primarily on the separate one-acre plot, extending only slightly across the former boundary between the two properties.Foreclosure triggered a legal dispute over the missing one-acre plotThe property was foreclosed in 2021 and was purchased by 5 AIF Juniper 2 LLC in the foreclosure auction. Thereafter, the entity filed legal proceedings in an attempt to prove its ownership and amend the deeds in such a way as to include the whole 8.25 acres in the deed. It claimed that there had been a mutual mistake which caused the failure of documents to reflect the initial intentions of the parties. The lower court ruled that the evidence was sufficient and the deeds should be amended to include both properties. Blackwell disagreed with the ruling, claiming that the deed should cover 7.25 acres only.Georgia Court of Appeals affirms ruling on the property deedsIn the case of Blackwell et al. v. 5 AIF Juniper 2, LLC, decided on 20 October 2026, the Georgia Court of Appeals affirmed the decision of the lower court. It was determined by the judges that there was enough evidence of the intent to sell the entire 8.25 acres. The purchase agreement referred to the house, while correspondence and closing records indicated that the lender had considered the residence and sought title insurance covering the combined property. Blackwell’s own testimony also established that he had taken steps to consolidate the two plots. The court affirmed the decision to correct the deeds to reflect the intended transaction.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Barack and Michelle Obama bought a $11.75 million Martha’s Vineyard mansion in 2019 with seven bedrooms, waterfront views and more than 29 acres of private land
articles.summary: Barack and Michelle Obama’s life after the White House has included a series of high-profile property purchases, with their Martha’s Vineyard home
articles.body: Barack and Michelle Obama’s life after the White House has included a series of high-profile property purchases, with their Martha’s Vineyard home offering a different setting from their former official residence in Washington. Bought for $11.75 million in December 2019, the Massachusetts estate sits on more than 29 acres in Edgartown, on the eastern side of the island. The property combines a substantial private house with open grounds, water views and space for outdoor recreation. The couple had spent time there during the summer before completing the purchase, according to reports at the time. Its size, secluded location and range of amenities set it apart from a conventional holiday home.The Obamas bought the Martha’s Vineyard estate for $11.75 million in 2019The Obamas acquired the property from Boston Celtics owner Wycliffe Grousbeck and his wife, Corinne Basler Grousbeck. The transaction was recorded with the local Registry of Deeds in December 2019, according to the Vineyard Gazette, which first reported the purchase.The reported price was considerably below the amount originally sought when the property entered the market in 2015. According to the reports, the estate had initially been offered for roughly twice what the Obamas eventually paid. The couple had reportedly made an offer in August 2019, following their summer stay at the house.The purchase added a sizeable coastal property to the couple's real estate holdings after Barack Obama left office in January 2017. Their Martha’s Vineyard home was not simply a place to stay during holidays. Its extensive grounds and multiple indoor and outdoor amenities offered room for family gatherings and longer stays away from their usual city residences.The Obamas’ Martha’s Vineyard mansion spans 29 acres with seven bedrooms and a poolThe estate covers more than 29 acres, giving the house a degree of separation from neighbouring properties. The main residence measures nearly 7,000 square feet and was reported to have seven bedrooms and eight and a half bathrooms when the sale was announced.The property’s layout is suited to accommodating several guests at once, with multiple bedrooms and bathrooms spread across a large private residence. Stone fireplaces feature among the interior details, while the grounds include a barn and a two-car garage. A swimming pool provides another leisure facility on the property.The combination of indoor space and open land distinguishes the estate from homes where the value rests mainly on the building itself. Here, the surrounding acreage is a substantial part of the appeal, providing room for outdoor activities while keeping the residence within its own expansive setting.Waterfront views and a quieter island settingThe property is in Edgartown, a historic town on Martha’s Vineyard, an island off the coast of Massachusetts. The estate’s location near the water gives it views of the surrounding coastal landscape, a feature that has helped make the island a popular summer destination for affluent homeowners and public figures.Martha’s Vineyard has a long association with seasonal retreats, but its appeal extends beyond the homes themselves. Beaches, sailing, small-town centres and access to the Atlantic coastline all contribute to its reputation as a summer escape. The Obamas had visited the island before buying the estate, making the eventual purchase a continuation of an existing connection rather than an entirely new destination.The acreage also offers a more private setting than a typical residential property in a town centre. While the house is large, the surrounding land gives the estate a different character from a conventional luxury home on a smaller plot.From the White House to private family residencesThe Martha’s Vineyard purchase formed part of the Obamas’ wider property portfolio after their time in Washington. They had previously bought a nine-bedroom home in the US capital for a reported $8.1 million, giving them a substantial residence in the city where Barack Obama had served two presidential terms.Their post-presidential years have also included commercial ventures in publishing and entertainment. Michelle Obama’s memoir Becoming became a major publishing release, while the couple reached a reported agreement with Netflix to develop programming.The island estate serves a different purpose from their Washington residence. Rather than being positioned in the political centre of the country, it offers a coastal setting with extensive private grounds.What makes the estate stand outThe reported $11.75 million price brought together several features often sought in high-end coastal real estate: a large residence, multiple bedrooms, water views and a substantial plot of land. The swimming pool, barn, garage and stone fireplaces add to the property’s range of facilities, while the acreage provides room around the main house.Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly available reports about Barack and Michelle Obama’s Martha’s Vineyard property purchase. articles.title: Omar Abdullah faces internal storm: Many NC MLAs upset over J&K cabinet rejig; Srinagar MP announces resignation
articles.summary: SRINAGAR: The government of chief minister Omar Abdullah is facing signs of discontent within the ruling National Conference (NC), with a number of
articles.body: SRINAGAR: The government of chief minister Omar Abdullah is facing signs of discontent within the ruling National Conference (NC), with a number of legislators reportedly unhappy over the recent cabinet expansion and seeking greater democracy within the party and resignation of the whole cabinet.The discontent within the party has taken place at a time when the party MP from Srinagar Aga Ruhullah Mehdi is resigning from the party on November 3 leaving Srinagar parliamentary seat open. “I will resign from the National Conference and my Lok Sabha seat on November 3, 2026. The crown prince and his cabal treat J&K as an estate passed down through the family. They expect the people to vote, then know their place. They take us for fools who cannot tell a broken promise from a political necessity. Ask them to honour their own manifesto, and they lecture us on how little we understand realpolitik,” Mehdi wrote on X.“We demanded the restoration of Article 370, the release of prisoners and the protection of our rights. They sought power on those promises, then treated us as fools for expecting them to deliver. We refuse to lend our name to this humiliation. There is no fixing this rot from within. The seat was won on a promise to the people,” Mehdi added. Mehdi said he would surrender the seat rather than become an accomplice to the betrayal of that promise.Mehdi would address the people on November 3, the death anniversary of his father, Aga Syed Mehdi, at Behisht-e-Zehra Park in Budgam. His father was a Congress leader and prominent Shiite cleric who was assassinated in a terrorist attack on November 3, 2000.Ruhullah Mehdi is an alumnus of Tyndale Biscoe School and holds a bachelor's degree in arts from the University of Kashmir. His political career began in 2002, when he contested and won his first Assembly election from Budgam. He retained the seat in 2008 and 2014. In 2009, he was inducted into the state Cabinet, becoming the youngest Cabinet minister. In 2015, Mehdi was nominated as the chief Spokesperson of the National Conference, the position he held for several years. However, after abrogation of Article 370 on August 5, 2019, he distanced himself from the party’s stand of maintaining silence over the situation in Jammu and Kashmir after August 5. He would urge the party to take a stand on Article 370 rather than urging the centre to restore statehood which he describes as a scaled down position.In August this year the NC president Dr Abdullah said Mehdi would not have won the parliamentary elections without the NC support. He said that if Mehdi believed Article 370 could be restored, he should fight for it, as no one had stopped him from pursuing the cause. Dr Abdullah had said the NC had not prevented Mehdi from pushing for the restoration of Article 370. Dr Abdullah had said Mehdi should resign and contest elections on his own. In response Mehdi had said that Dr Abdullah has for the first time asked anything from him and he will not disappoint him.MLAs meetingMeanwhile, according to the sources, over a dozen party legislators met Friday evening at the residence of Qaiser Jamshaid Lone, who represents the Lolab constituency, with several others joining the meeting online. They decided to seek resignation of the entire council of ministers and demand that a new cabinet be formed through consensus, based on merit and in keeping with democratic principles, sources said. They also decided to seek the resignation of the chief minister’s advisor Nasir Ahmad Wani.In a related development, NC president Dr Farooq Abdullah removed Mubarak Gul as the party’s general secretary. Gul was among the MLAs who attended the meeting at Lone’s residence. After the cabinet expansion on Tuesday, Dr Abdullah had elevated Gul, who wanted cabinet induction for himself, to the post of general secretary.Omar Abdullah and Dr. Farooq Abdullah are in New Delhi.Dismissing reports of widespread discontent within the party and rebellion, NC spokesperson Ifra Jan questioned the claim that 20 MLAs attended the meeting at Lone’s residence. “They are saying 20 MLAs held this particular meeting. Where is this figure of 20 coming from? Is there a photograph or a list of names? Somebody anonymously claims 20 and everyone else repeats it without any investigative corroboration,” she said.“After the cabinet expansion, I think one or two MLAs openly expressed their displeasure and that was there for everyone to see. Isn’t that normal? Doesn’t this happen in all political parties? Some MLAs are happy while others are unhappy. This is common practice across the country,” she said.“Ever since Omar Sahib (Omar Abdullah) took oath, the leader of the opposition BJP's Sunil Sharma, has been claiming that the government will fall next week. Unfortunately, nobody is asking why. Every disagreement is being viewed through the prism of “government will fall rumours” without any evidence. We consider any claim of large-scale discontent within the party as a rumour,” she added. Sunil Sharma said it seems Omar Abdullah government has only eight MLAs with it and those eight are cabinet Ministers.Nazir Gurezi, who was part of the meeting, told the TOI that Lone had invited all MLAs and “large number of MLAs were at his residence. We just had food there”.On Tuesday morning Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha administered the oath of office and secrecy to the newly inducted ministers, Ali Mohammad Sagar, Shamima Firdous, Mir Saifullah and Altaf Ahmad Kaloo at Lok Bhawan in Srinagar taking the number to eight with Omar including nine. Omar dropped Satish Sharma, who was Minister for food, consumer affairs, transport science, IT, youth affairs, sports, and training.Omar was sworn in as chief minister on October 16, 2024, along with five ministers. Under the prescribed norms, the council of Ministers cannot exceed 10% of the total strength of the legislative assembly. With 90 members, the Jammu and Kashmir Assembly can have a maximum of nine ministers, including the chief minister. Three cabinet berths had remained vacant for nearly two years as the party struggled to decide whom to induct.Soon after the expansion on Tuesday, NC MLA Abdul Majeed Larmi broke down. “I deserved a place in the cabinet. I felt very sad not to be part of the cabinet. I was deserving of it (cabinet seat). Till the last moment, I was expecting to be part of the cabinet,” Larmi said. “I am a law graduate, while the MLA chosen has not even passed matriculation,” he had said.Mubarak Gul’s supporters lodged a protest at the party headquarters.In the 90-member Assembly, the NC has 41 MLAs and is backed by six independent legislators, while the Congress, with six MLAs, extends support to the government from outside.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: US jails two Chinese nationals for spying
articles.summary: Liren Lai and Yuance Chen admitted to facilitating ‘dead drop’ cash payments worth at least $30,000 to people in the US.
articles.body:
Two Chinese nationals have been jailed in the United States after admitting to trying to recruit US military service members to spy for Beijing.

Liren “Ryan” Lai, 40, and Yuance Chen, 39, were each sentenced to 30 months in prison and three years of supervised release, the US Department of Justice (DOJ) said in a statement on Friday.

The men sought to arrange “dead drop” cash payments in exchange for information related to US national security, the statement also said.

The pair operated a “long-running”, “extensive” and “brazen” scheme to undermine US national security and support Chinese intelligence operations and recruitment in the US, Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A Eisenberg said.

According to court documents, Lai and Chen began acting as agents of China’s foreign intelligence arm, the Ministry of State Security, no later than May 2021.

Lai, who arrived in the US on a tourist visa, recruited Chen, a permanent resident, into the scheme and initially served as an intermediary between Chen and intelligence officers – until Chen was able to receive his orders directly from his handler.

In May 2022, they facilitated a secret cash payment of $10,000 from China, ordering US-based individuals to drop the cash at a specified location for collection by someone else, an arrangement known as a “dead drop”.

The two later carried out another similar operation, facilitating a payment of $20,000.

Chen and Lai also engaged in other forms of espionage, including obtaining photographs of a naval facility, military recruits, and active-duty sailors. Chen collected personal information about a US Navy employee and maintained detailed biographical information about military personnel who were potential intelligence targets.

The DOJ did not say how many times the pair had facilitated payments, nor how many people they had successfully recruited in the US.

The men were found guilty of two charges: conspiracy to act as agents of a foreign government without prior notification to the Attorney General; and acting as agents of a foreign government without prior notification.

The pair were arrested and charged in June 2025.

In late August, US President Donald Trump said he knew China spied on the US, but “we spy on them too”.

In June, China announced that it had arrested a US citizen accused of espionage a day after US media reports said a scholar holding dual US and Myanmar citizenship was detained in early June.

The scholar, Min Zin, previously wrote opinion pieces on Myanmar politics that were critical of the military government, as well as the opposition groups it is fighting.

articles.title: A Vermont dam built in the early 1900s to feed a private trout pond was breached in 2011; crews removed its remains in 2018, reopening 87 miles of stream
articles.summary: In 2018, crews removed the remnants of the Killooleet Dam, restoring fish passage along 87 miles of Vermont's Hancock Branch of the White River, allowing aquatic life to thrive once more.
articles.body: A dam constructed in Vermont in the early 1900s to provide water to a private trout fishing pond eventually turned into an obstruction to fish movement while disrupting the natural flow of a stream. The Killooleet Dam, located on the Hancock Branch of the White River near Camp Killooleet, was damaged by back-to-back floods before Tropical Storm Irene breached it in August 2011. This destroyed most of the structure, but concrete remnants stayed in the waterway, thus constricting the channel and preventing the stream from accessing the floodplain along its northern bank. After seven years, the White River Partnership (WRP) and its partners removed those remaining materials and carried out further channel improvements. The project reopened 87 miles of stream to fish passage.A dam built for a private trout pondThe Killooleet Dam was actually constructed in the early 1900s to feed a private trout fishing pond. As per reports, the estate was associated with a trout fishing club before becoming the site of a summer camp. During the major 1927 flood, the dam was reportedly damaged. It was, however, subsequently rebuilt when the camp was established. Camp Killooleet was established by Margaret Bartlett and Toni Taylor in 1927, with the Seeger family later taking ownership of the property.The structure suffered further damage during the flooding in 2008. Another major breach was caused by Tropical Storm Irene in August 2011. While the dam was no longer intact, its concrete remains continued to block part of the Hancock Branch. Thus, the problem was not just the presence of an obsolete dam, but the effects of the damaged structure that remained in the waterbody.The 2015 Upper and Middle White River Watershed Corridor Plan listed the removal of the destroyed dam as a high-priority project. Additionally, it identified that there was a separate requirement to improve the Hancock Branch’s connection with its floodplain. The plan noted that remnants of the old concrete structure created a channel constriction, while the affected area lacked some of the features needed for a more stable and diverse stream channel.Removing the concrete remnants in 2018The WRP received funding to develop priority projects identified in the corridor plan in 2017. Kate Seeger, who owned the Camp Killooleet property, expressed interest in working with the partnership on dam removal and floodplain restoration. The engineering design to help move the work forward was funded by her. The WRP subsequently joined hands with engineering firm Ripple Natural Resources and received funding from Vermont’s Ecosystem Restoration Program to implement the in-stream projects in 2018.Construction took place between August and September 2018. Harvey’s Excavating broke apart the remaining concrete dam structure and removed those pieces from the Hancock Branch in August. Following this, the contractor reportedly built three channel-spanning rock weirs along a 500-foot stretch of the stream. They used large stones and native rocks that were found at the site. While separate, they were complementary parts of the restoration: removing the concrete eliminated the old obstruction, while the rock structures helped reshape the channel.The rock weirs created pools and added roughness to the channel, improving the variety of in-stream habitat. They also raised the streambed elevation, which helped Hancock Branch reconnect with the adjacent floodplain along its northern bank.Reopening 87 miles to fish passageRemoving the Killooleet Dam remnants restored fish passage along 87 miles of stream, as noted by the WRP. The total comprises 36 miles upstream and 51 miles downstream of the former dam site. Rather than implying that the crews carried out construction across all 87 miles, the figure refers to the connected stream network made accessible to fish after the obstruction was eliminated.Connected waterways allow fish to move between various parts of a river system to access feeding areas, spawning grounds and other habitats. Structures like dams and other barriers can interrupt those movements. The US Fish and Wildlife Service describes fish passage as the ability of aquatic species to move freely through waterways during their life cycles. Removing such barriers can reconnect habitats that were previously separated.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Chola-era bronze idols of Nataraja, Sivakami unearthed at Nagapattinam
articles.summary: CHENNAI: The Tamil Nadu archaeology department has unearthed two Chola-era bronze idols of Nataraja and Sivakami during an excavation in Nagapattinam, a
articles.body: CHENNAI: The Tamil Nadu archaeology department has unearthed two Chola-era bronze idols of Nataraja and Sivakami during an excavation in Nagapattinam, a major port city during the period.The iconography and artistry suggest that the idols date back to the 12th century. The Cholas ruled the region from the 9th to the 13th century CE. Archaeology minister A Rajmohan announced the discovery on Friday.The idols were found at a depth of 1m. The Nataraja idol, which is 110cm tall and 100cm wide, depicts Lord Shiva with four arms in the 'ananda tandava' pose. The lower right hand is in the 'abhaya mudra', the upper right hand holds a drum, the upper left hand carries a flame, and the lower left hand displays the 'gajahasta mudra'. One foot rests on the demon Muyalaka, while the other is raised.The Sivakami idol is 82cm tall and 23cm wide. It is depicted in the 'tribhanga' posture. The right hand displays the 'kataka mudra', while the left shows the 'dolahasta mudra'. Both idols were found on pedestals.“These are two masterpieces of Chola-period bronzes with fine workmanship. They may have been buried for safekeeping,” said Professor K Rajan, adviser to the state archaeology department.K Vasanthakumar, who led the excavation, said the team was looking for clues to understand why hundreds of Chola-era bronzes had been buried in Nagapattinam. The two idols have been brought to Chennai for chemical treatment, while metallurgical analysis will determine the composition of the materials used.V Selvakumar, a retired professor in the department of maritime history and marine archaeology at Tamil University, said Nagapattinam was a multifaceted urban centre during the Chola period, with a port, manufacturing units, active merchant guilds and craft workers, military and naval facilities, as well as several religious shrines.“The port city was frequented by traders, pilgrims and diplomats. articles.title: Olusola Olonade: Meet the Nigerian woman who became first-time mother at 50, welcoming quadruplets: ‘I never knew I would have four at once’
articles.summary: For a lot of women, there’s a ticking clock attached to marriage and motherhood: it’s a sense that if you don’t follow the schedule everyone expects,
articles.body: For a lot of women, there’s a ticking clock attached to marriage and motherhood: it’s a sense that if you don’t follow the schedule everyone expects, you’re falling behind. That’s why Olusola Olonade’s story lands with such force. She turned her own life’s timeline upside down, getting married at 48 and, just as she was about to turn 50, becoming a mother for the first time — not to one baby, but to four.“I gave birth at the age of 50, but I didn’t expect four children at once,” she told BBC Africa. She sounded both stunned and amused by what had transpired. Her journey hasn’t just captured the attention of people online for the sheer novelty of quadruplets. It’s resonated because it’s about asking for more out of life when everyone else assumes your window of opportunity has closed. Her story winds through the worlds of faith, modern fertility medicine, the unpredictability of biology, and an unwavering belief that life can still surprise you, even in your fifties.Olusola delivered her quadruplets — two girls, two boys — on March 6, 2026, about three weeks shy of her 50th birthday. This wasn’t some improbable accident, either; she conceived through IVF, a procedure that involves fertilising the egg outside the body before transferring the embryo back into the uterus. If her journey to marriage had been long, her wait for motherhood felt turbocharged. When she and her husband decided they wanted children, she pushed forward. “I’ve waited for a husband, I don’t want to wait for children,” she remembers thinking. And she didn’t.Olusola Olonade: Who is she?By her own account, Olonade (born Olusola Adeniji) never spent much time worrying she would remain childless. She had faith in God’s promise, in her husband’s family history (which she’d researched carefully), and, crucially, in the science she trusted to help her. She also knew there were no guarantees; she’d seen women younger than her try IVF multiple times, only to be left disappointed. She knew this could’ve ended differently, maybe with an empty nursery rather than four squirming babies.But instead, her path turned almost comically unexpected. At her first ultrasound, the doctor said twins. Later, someone else spotted triplets. On another visit, quadruplets. At that point, she joked she wouldn’t be coming in for any more scans: what if they found a fifth? The confusion didn’t just make for a good story. It captured something real about pregnancy, especially one brought about by fertility treatments. Multiple embryos, split-second readings, constantly shifting counts — it really can turn into a guessing game. Through it all, Olonade’s amazement kept rising. By the time she went into labour, she clung to hope that her four would all make it to birth safely.Finally, on March 6, she made it: two boys and two girls. She marked the occasion, not just privately but in the company of her community, offering thanks at church, holding her four babies, her faith and her happiness out for everyone to see. The joy was unmistakable, but so was a sense of groundedness. She knows how rare this outcome is. IVF is remarkable, yes, but it’s not a guarantee. She’s said so herself: sometimes, it just doesn’t work, even after multiple tries.What are the risks of pregnancy with quadruplets at 50?As for the medical side of things, quadruplet pregnancies are never simple, and having babies at 50 brings another layer of complexity. The risks run higher: preterm labour, low birth weights, complications for the mother, a greater need for medical intervention, and constant monitoring along the way. None of that was lost on Olonade’s doctors: more scans, more specialists, and preparations for whatever might happen. She hasn’t disclosed the details of her babies’ births, like their weights or whether they spent time in neonatal care, but she’s said the delivery was safe. For her and her husband, that’s clearly the headline.Notably, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) agrees that IVF can result in multiple pregnancies, particularly when more than one embryo is transferred. It also explains that the likelihood of multiple pregnancy can be higher among older women. The Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine recommends careful monitoring of pregnancies achieved through IVF because of the additional risks that may be involved.Olonade’s story is not just about the birth, though. It’s also about what comes after, about building a life that’s equal parts chaos and deep gratitude. Olonade describes her husband as someone who steps in fully, even pulling night shifts with the babies so she can rest. He sees her as the answer to a prayer for peace and companionship. Their late-in-life marriage, now bolstered by the chaos of four young children, seems to have helped them find the kind of partnership they both wanted.Olusola Olonade’s life now: ‘I want to live to become a great-grandmother’You get the sense from Olonade that she’s looking far beyond the early months of diapers and feedings. She talks openly about her wish, not just to see her children grow, but to watch them become parents themselves, maybe even to become a great-grandmother. There’s a defiance in the way she describes her hopes. She points to other women who, through sheer resilience, have lived to see generation after generation. Why not me, she seems to say.That’s a big part of why Olonade’s story lingers for so many people. She’s not just defying the logic of biology; she’s defying the expectations society presses down on women: about age, fertility, marriage, and what’s “supposed” to be possible after a certain point. She’s proof that the journey to family can wind in unpredictable directions, that there are second acts (and third, and fourth), and that sometimes, when you stop believing the timeline matters, life brings you something you never expected, or, in Olusola’s case, four somethings at once!You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Coup d'etat' or rule of law? Why Poland's PM and president are locked in a bitter standoff
articles.summary: Poland was plunged into a fresh constitutional crisis on Friday after the president of its Constitutional Tribunal, Bogdan Święczkowski, and his deputy,
articles.body: Poland was plunged into a fresh constitutional crisis on Friday after the president of its Constitutional Tribunal, Bogdan Święczkowski, and his deputy, Bartłomiej Sochański, were suspended for a month, prompting riot police deployment outside the court in Warsaw.President Karol Nawrocki cut short his flight to Senegal and returned to Poland as the confrontation between prime minister Donald Tusk's government and the opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party intensified.The crisis centres on competing claims over the legitimacy of judicial appointments and the government's efforts to reverse changes introduced during PiS's previous tenure.Why were the judges suspended?Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska issued the one-month suspension against Święczkowski and Sochański, accusing them of blocking legally appointed judges, including herself, from participating in court proceedings.Justice minister Waldemar Żurek also said he had requested that the two judges' immunity be lifted to enable criminal proceedings against them.According to the Associated Press, police were deployed after concerns were raised about the safety of judges and administrative staff. Officers prevented protesters from entering the building. Police said three people were detained after demonstrators breached the court's fence and threw objects at officers.The Constitutional Tribunal disputed the suspension, maintaining that its existing leadership remained legally appointed."All persons participating in these actions are committing the crime of a coup d'etat," the court said in a social media statement.Why are Tusk and Nawrocki fighting?The dispute dates back to 2015, when the nationalist Law and Justice appointed judges to positions that critics said had already been lawfully filled. European courts subsequently questioned the independence of the tribunal, with the European Union imposing fines on Poland over judicial reforms.Tusk's pro-European coalition came to power in 2023, promising to restore judicial independence. However, Nawrocki, who is backed by PiS, has resisted several appointments, including refusing to swear in judges selected by parliament.Earlier this year, Nawrocki refused to swear in three of six judges nominated by parliament. Meanwhile, Tribunal president Bogdan Święczkowski, a former deputy justice minister under the PiS government, declined to allow judges elected by the current parliamentary majority to take their seats.Defending his government's actions, Tusk wrote on X, "Restoring the rule of law is our duty. After years of lawlessness under PiS, this is a difficult process, sometimes painful, and it requires decisive action. There is no other way."Speaking to ANI, Poland's deputy prime minister and foreign minister Radosław Sikorski said, "The outgoing president was preventing the duly elected majority from working—from passing judgments, interpreting laws, or even adopting their own budget. Therefore, action had to be taken to enable the Tribunal to function once again."Nawrocki returns as opposition alleges coupNawrocki cancelled his Senegal visit mid-flight, writing on X, "At such a moment, the President must be in Poland. I'm interrupting my flight to Senegal. I'm returning."A video shared by Constitutional Tribunal Judge Maciej Berek on X showed Polish president Karol Nawrocki pushing his way past judges gathered at the tribunal’s entrance, prompting a clarification from Berek over what he described as an “outrageous and scandalous situation”.Berek said the judges had been waiting to greet Nawrocki and invite him into a room prepared for the meeting. He alleged that the president “crashed into Judge A. Korwin-Piotrowska with force” before pushing through the group. “I emphasize—no one grabbed the President, nor did anyone tussle with the President,” he wrote, adding that the clips published did not show the entire incident.Meanwhile, other videos circulating on X showed Nawrocki confronting Anna Korwin-Piotrowska. He said, “You are not judge of the Constitutional Court!”PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński accused the government of authoritarianism, saying, "From today, Poland becomes a police state, and from there there is already a direct path to authoritarianism, and then to totalitarianism."You use AI every day. articles.title: 'He was crying and grabbing the doctor's hands to stop him': US organ donation group faces decertification after Kentucky man’s near-fatal ordeal
articles.summary: “My brother grabbed the doctor’s hand as he tried to harvest his organs…” Donna Rhorer’s account of what happened to her brother, Anthony Thomas “TJ”
articles.body: “My brother grabbed the doctor’s hand as he tried to harvest his organs…” Donna Rhorer’s account of what happened to her brother, Anthony Thomas “TJ” Hoover II, has become central to a case raising serious questions about patient safety and oversight in the US organ donation system. Hoover, who was taken for organ donation after a drug overdose in Kentucky in October 2021, showed signs of life as preparations for organ retrieval progressed. Nearly five years later, the case has drawn renewed scrutiny after US authorities moved to decertify Network for Hope, the organisation responsible for coordinating organ donations in the region.The US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) announced on August 5, 2026, that it had begun the process of decertifying Network for Hope following federal reviews that identified concerning patient-safety practices in multiple cases involving potential organ donors. Rhorer described her experience in testimony at the Kentucky Attorney General’s office, recounting how her family had been told that Hoover had no reflexes or brain activity and would not recover. They agreed to withdraw life support and honour his wishes to become an organ donor. However, she said, his behaviour during the subsequent preparations raised questions about whether he was still alive.“I was there, I saw what happened to my brother. They prepared to recover his organs while he was still alive. During that honour walk his eyes were open, he was tracking me and they told me it was just reflex,” Rhorer testified.“And then during the heart cath, he was thrashing, crying and grabbing the doctor's hands to stop him. Even after those signs the organ procurement continued until the physician refused to proceed.”Rhorer also alleged that a coordinator contacted the organisation’s home office after the doctor refused to continue, only to be told to find another surgeon or risk losing her job. “One of the organisation’s own coordinators called the home office after the doctor refused, she was told, ‘find another surgeon or you'll lose your job because we're finishing this case. My brother almost died that day, that should never happen to anyone. Laws and standards were clearly violated, those responsible must be held accountable,” she said.When the procedure was stopped, Rhorer said, the family was told to take Hoover home and make him comfortable because he was not expected to survive much longer.“Well, it's been five years, and he's still here. I'm grateful every day for that but he is not the same, he has nightmares, he struggles remembering things and he asked me 'sis, why do they wanna kill me?' I don't have an answer for him,” she said.Procedure stopped, but questions remainedHoover’s case came to wider public attention in October 2024, when NPR reported accounts from witnesses who said he had shown signs of life during preparations for organ recovery. The Guardian also reported on the incident, including the concerns raised by former employees of the Kentucky Organ Donor Affiliates (KODA), the organisation now known as Network for Hope.Former KODA employee Nyckoletta Martin and organ-preservationist Natasha Miller raised concerns about Hoover’s condition. Miller, whose work involved preserving organs after removal, reportedly witnessed Hoover thrashing and crying on the operating table. Other accounts described him moving his head and pulling his knees towards his chest.The organ retrieval was ultimately stopped after a physician refused to proceed. Rhorer said the family was not initially given a full explanation of what had happened. She later learned more about the incident after a former KODA employee contacted her in January 2024.Hoover survived, but his family has described lasting difficulties with memory and other aspects of his daily life. Rhorer’s account has since become part of a wider debate over the responsibilities of organ procurement organisations (OPOs), which coordinate donations between hospitals, potential donors and transplant centres.Federal investigation identifies wider concernsThe controversy intensified after federal authorities examined hundreds of cases handled by Network for Hope. In its August 5, 2026 announcement, HHS said the Health Resources and Services Administration had reviewed 351 cases between 2021 and 2024 in which organ donation had been authorised but ultimately did not proceed.Of those cases, 103 had concerning features, according to the department. It said 73 patients displayed neurological signs incompatible with organ donation. The review raised concerns about neurological assessments, communication between medical teams, consent practices and the classification of causes of death, particularly in cases involving drug overdoses.The findings do not mean that organs were removed from all the patients reviewed. Instead, they point to concerns about the assessments and preparations undertaken before donation could proceed. Organ recovery must follow the applicable medical and legal requirements for determining death.US authorities move to decertify Network for HopeFollowing the federal review, HHS said Network for Hope had failed to demonstrate sufficient improvement despite earlier corrective measures and monitoring. Authorities therefore began the process of decertifying the organisation, which coordinates organ procurement across Kentucky and parts of Indiana, Ohio and West Virginia.The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services issued a notice stating that its Medicare agreement with Network for Hope would be terminated on November 3, 2026, subject to the applicable process. The organisation’s donation service area is expected to be transferred through a process that depends on the outcome of any appeal or the organisation’s decision not to appeal.Network for Hope has disputed aspects of the allegations and maintained that organ procurement organisations do not provide patient care or independently declare death. The organisation has also said that organ recovery can proceed only after an independent healthcare provider has declared a patient dead.The regulatory action has placed renewed focus on how hospitals and organ procurement organisations communicate with families, assess neurological activity and respond when relatives or medical staff raise concerns about a patient’s condition.The United States has more than 100,000 people waiting for organ transplants, making public confidence in the donation system critical. Experts and transplant advocates have stressed the importance of investigating alleged failures thoroughly while ensuring that individual cases do not discourage people from donating organs that could save lives.For Rhorer, however, the issue remains deeply personal. Her brother survived the procedure that was meant to lead to organ recovery, but she says he continues to live with the consequences of what happened. His case has now become part of a wider examination of patient safety and accountability in the US organ donation system.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
